newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yogic flyers hop for peace at Bonn conference.
newsitem.headline: Yogic flyers hop for peace at Bonn conference.

text.p: Yogic flyers from Natural Law Parties around the world gathered in Bonn on Friday to bounce for peace, pledging to combat global crime, disease, war and unemployment with meditation and levitation.

"First one practises transcendental meditation and calms down," Bevan Morris, head of Australia's Natural Law Party, told the hundreds of delegates at the group's fourth annual congress in Bonn as some of the devotees began a demonstration.
"Then one lifts up in a series of hops that are very delightful for the yogic flyer," he said. "But that is just the beginning. Eventually one can learn to levitate."
A group of 23 yogic flyers, clad in white trousers and T-shirts decorated with the party's rainbow symbol, sat cross-legged on a foam mat with their eyes closed.

After a few minutes of meditation, the flyers began to shake, giggle and hop across the mat on their knees, bouncing about half a metre off the ground and often colliding with each other as they projected themselves forward.
The Natural Law Party was founded in Britain five years ago by Maharishi Mahesh Yogi and says it now has branches and millions of adherents in 60 countries worldwide.

"Yogic flying is enormously beneficial for the individual producing maximum coherence in brain functioning," said John Hagelin, the party's U.S. presidential candidate in 1995, before settling down for his daily hop.

Hagelin, a physicist by profession, said sociological studies had shown dramatic social improvements if the 'square root of one percent' of the population practised transcendental meditation and yogic flying every morning and evening.
"This group will radiate peace and harmony to everyone in Bonn," said Morris.
"A group of seven to ten thousand flyers would produce a positive effect on the whole world."

Reinhard Borowitz, Secretary General of the Maharishi Council of Natural Law Parties, said the group wanted to set up specially trained teams of yogic flyers around the world, a "Vedic Peace Corps", to do away with the need for national armies and weapons.
He said NATO and the European Union were making grave errors with plans to absorb members from the former communist East.
"Russia feels cornered and pushed back. We know that the expansion will just increase tensions," Borowitz said.
Zuzana Sojhova, the group's leader in the Czech Republic, said her country did not want to join the EU and NATO.
"We have somehow allowed the intervention of Western military powers into our countries, but we can defend ourselves perfectly well with the help of a Vedic Peace Corps," she said.
The party's leader in Poland, Andre Michaelovski, agreed.

"The Natural Law Party of Poland does not want the country to join the EU and NATO and be used as a tool to create tension," he said. "We propose the creation of a new profession in the military -- yogic flyers for world peace."
